newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1996 privatisation revenue PLN 2.3 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1996 privatisation revenue PLN 2.3 mln.

text.p: Sales of state-owned companies brought 2.3 billion zlotys to the national budget last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said on Thursday.

The so-called capital privatisation, which embraces flotations, direct sales of shares to strategic investors and involves state-owned firms functioning as joint-stock companies, generated 1.9 billion zlotys, said Maria Sierpinska, GUS' enterprises department official.
"The capital privatisation brought 1.9 billion zlotys, or eight percent more than envisaged by the budget law," Sierpinska told a news conference.

She said that the direct method of privatisation, in which small firms directly supervised by ministries or provincial governors are sold through simplified procedures, brought nearly 400 million zlotys.
She said that since the 1990 launch of sell-offs 5,592 state-owned companies were privatised, liquidated or prepared for privatisation out the then existing more than 8,000.
She said 1,227 state-owned companies had been turned into tresury-owned joint-stock companies of which 151 were sold to selected investors or floated.
Sierpinska said that 2,970 state-owned companies existed in Poland at the end of 1996.
Poland's private sector generates more than 60 percent of gross domestic product and employs more than 60 percent of the workforce.
